examples.question_text: Classify $f(x)=\arcsin x$ and $g(x)=\arctan x$ as odd, even or neither. Give an algebraic reason for each classification.
examples.solution_text:
For $-1\le x\le1$,
$\begin{aligned}f(-x)&=\arcsin(-x)\\&=-\arcsin x\\&=-f(x).\end{aligned}$
For every real $x$,
$\begin{aligned}g(-x)&=\arctan(-x)\\&=-\arctan x\\&=-g(x).\end{aligned}$
Both functions are odd because replacing the input by its negative reverses the sign of the output throughout their domains.

The points $\left(1,\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$ and $\left(-1,-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$ map to each other under a $180^{\circ}$ rotation about the origin.
The same relationship holds for every point because $\arctan(-x)=-\arctan x$ for every real $x$. The graph has rotational symmetry about the origin, so the function is odd.

Let $\theta=\arccos x$, where $-1\le x\le1$. Then $\cos\theta=x$ and $0\le\theta\le\pi$.
$\cos(\pi-\theta)=-\cos\theta=-x$.
Since $\pi-\theta$ also lies in $[0,\pi]$,
$\arccos(-x)=\pi-\arccos x$.
The endpoint values are $f(-1)=\pi$ and $f(1)=0$. They are neither equal nor negatives of each other, so the function is neither even nor odd.
The identity gives $\arccos(-x)+\arccos x=\pi$. Its centre of rotational symmetry is $\left(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$; oddness requires rotational symmetry about the origin.

examples.question_text:
Simplify each expression using inverse trigonometric identities. State any domain restriction.
(a) $4\arctan(-x)+\arctan x$
(b) $\arccos(-x)+\arccos x$
(c) $\arccos(-x)+2\arcsin(-x)+2\arcsin x$
examples.solution_text:
(a) For every real $x$,
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}4\arctan(-x)+\arctan x\\&=4(-\arctan x)+\arctan x\\&=-3\arctan x.\end{aligned}$
(b) For $-1\le x\le1$,
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\arccos(-x)+\arccos x\\&=(\pi-\arccos x)+\arccos x\\&=\pi.\end{aligned}$
(c) For $-1\le x\le1$,
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\arccos(-x)+2\arcsin(-x)+2\arcsin x\\&=(\pi-\arccos x)-2\arcsin x+2\arcsin x\\&=\pi-\arccos x.\end{aligned}$

(a) Use the negative-argument identities.
$\begin{aligned}\arcsin\left(-\frac12\right)&=-\arcsin\frac12\\&=-\frac{\pi}{6}.\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\arccos\left(-\frac12\right)&=\pi-\arccos\frac12\\&=\pi-\frac{\pi}{3}\\&=\frac{2\pi}{3}.\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\arctan\left(-\frac1{\sqrt3}\right)&=-\arctan\frac1{\sqrt3}\\&=-\frac{\pi}{6}.\end{aligned}$
(b) Substitute these principal values.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3\arcsin\left(-\frac12\right)-\arccos\left(-\frac12\right)+\arcsin\frac12\\&=3\left(-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)-\frac{2\pi}{3}+\frac{\pi}{6}\\&=-\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{2\pi}{3}\\&=-\pi.\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Use parity identities to evaluate:
(a) $\arctan\left(-\frac12\right)$;
(b) $\arctan\left(-\frac12\right)+\arccos(-1)$.
Work in radians and give each answer correct to three decimal places. Retain full calculator precision until the final rounding.
examples.solution_text:
(a)
$\begin{aligned}\arctan\left(-\frac12\right)&=-\arctan\frac12\\&=-0.4636476090\ldots\\&\approx-0.464.\end{aligned}$
(b) $\arccos(-1)=\pi-\arccos1=\pi$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\arctan\left(-\frac12\right)+\arccos(-1)\\&=\pi-\arctan\frac12\\&=2.6779450445\ldots\\&\approx2.678.\end{aligned}$
Both answers are rounded to three decimal places.

examples.derivation: The supplied negative-argument identities give f(-x)=-f(x) on [-1,1] for arcsine and g(-x)=-g(x) on the real numbers for arctangent. Both domains are symmetric about zero, so both functions are odd.

arctan(1)=pi/4 and arctan(-1)=-pi/4. Rotation about the origin sends (1,pi/4) to (-1,-pi/4). The negative-argument identity establishes this relationship throughout the domain. The TikZ plots arctangent in radians with horizontal asymptotes at ±pi/2; solution coordinates are absent from the prompt diagram.

For theta=arccos(x), theta lies in [0,pi]. Since cos(pi-theta)=-x and pi-theta remains in that interval, arccos(-x)=pi-arccos(x). At x=1, f(-1)=pi differs from both f(1)=0 and -f(1)=0, rejecting evenness and oddness. Paired outputs sum to pi, establishing rotational symmetry about (0,pi/2). The parametrisation (cos(t),t), 0≤t≤pi, correctly draws arccosine.

For real x, 4arctan(-x)+arctan(x)=(-4+1)arctan(x)=-3arctan(x). On [-1,1], arccos(-x)+arccos(x)=pi. On the same domain, the two arcsine terms cancel after replacing arcsin(-x) with -arcsin(x), leaving pi-arccos(x). Each bare opening expression has the required phantom equals gutter.

The negative-argument identities give arcsin(-1/2)=-pi/6, arccos(-1/2)=pi-pi/3=2pi/3 and arctan(-1/sqrt(3))=-pi/6. The combination equals -3pi/6-2pi/3+pi/6=-pi/3-2pi/3=-pi. Independent equations use relation alignment; the bare combination uses a phantom equals gutter.
arctan(-1/2)=-0.463647609000806… rounds to -0.464. With arccos(-1)=pi, the sum is pi-arctan(1/2)=2.677945044588987… and rounds to 2.678. Both use radians and retain precision until final rounding.
